Step 9 complete. `research/frontier-17-alpha-step9.md` is written.

**Sweep result: 94 declines examined against disk, 3 overturned and built, 2 records corrected, 91 upheld, 0 open ledger rows.**

Two structural facts first: every one of the run's 43 `deferred` rows named a destination (the prose-only-decline failure mode does not occur here), and all 16 destinations outside this run are unwritten planned pages — no decline defers a result to an already-published page that would never be retro-filled.

**Built:**
- `ex-orthogonal-group-is-a-regular-level-set` — the decline claimed O(n) "uses Lie-group and manifold structure". False: `A ↦ AᵀA` is a polynomial map between Euclidean spaces, `H = ½AS` witnesses surjectivity, and the page's own regular-level-set corollary delivers the n(n−1)/2 graph. It is the pair's only example with a codomain of dimension > 1 — the only place the vector-valued normal form does work.
- `ex-lagrange-multipliers-with-two-constraints` — deferred to its own pair's companion page, i.e. nowhere. The A page's vector-valued multiplier theorem had no worked example at all; its only one exercised the q=1 corollary.
- `cor-index-of-a-full-rank-integer-sublattice-is-the-absolute-determinant` — declined `out-of-scope` with no destination, on a page that proves Smith normal form and covers ℤ-modules. Neighbouring covolume declines are correct; this one was swept along and needs no volume.

**A refuter caught a fatal defect in my own work.** I claimed the fourth multiplier solution was neither a maximum nor a minimum. It is a **strict local maximum** — s = −√2 is an endpoint of the range of s on the circle, which is precisely why. The title and Example asserted more than the verification gave. Repaired by correcting the claim: the item now proves local maximality via ‖p−P₄‖² = 2+√2·s, and the lesson is restated as the multiplier equation failing to separate local from global. The `endpoints` boundary row had *recorded* the false claim as its evidence. Two nonfatal findings also applied (undefined "critical point"; a title generalising past its statement, fixed by adding the converse clause from the simultaneous basis theorem rather than narrowing).

Two records corrected without a build: D54's destination named a page whose subject (2-dimensional patches in ℝ³) cannot carry an n-ball's surface measure — retargeted to the Hausdorff page; D43's self-referential deferral reclassified.

**One thing for you.** D53, Legendre duplication, is deferred to the unwritten complex `the-gamma-function` page under a real/complex seam recorded at step 3 — but its positive-real case is one lemma from the page's own Bohr–Mollerup theorem. The decline's own text concedes this. It stands on a true claim, so I did not overturn a settled reading-order decision at step 9; it is yours to revisit. D1, D45, D68 are the run's three explicit `owner-decision` declines.

All gates green except judge closure, which names exactly the three new items (`unadjudicated 0`, `open_fatal 0`, no page-mate staled). I did not run the sweep — that is the gate's mechanical repair.
